## 3. Demo director

Two counts are reported, and the difference between them matters.

- **18 family keys** over **17 distinct families**.
  `subagent` is an alias of `agent`: the contract names the family one way and this harness
  named it another, and both resolve so either vocabulary works.
- **133 events across family keys** — the raw number, inflated, because
  the alias family is counted a second time and several event names are second names bound to
  one function — versus **120 distinct behaviours**, which is the number of
  things the Director can actually do.

| | fired | ok | failed | changed the store | changed the DOM | inert |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| raw | 133 | 133 | **0** | 79 | 45 | 54 |
| distinct | 120 | 120 | **0** | 77 | 45 | 43 |

"Inert" is not a failure. Some triggers restore a state that is already current, and a trigger
that honestly does nothing is better than one that reports a change it did not make.

### The fourteen states the packet names

Nine of the fourteen are also family names here; five are not, and those five are the reason
this table exists. The mapping is declared in `tools/drive.mjs` and then checked against the
sweep, so a state counts as covered only when one of its events actually fired.

**14 of 14 covered.**

| packet state | events fired ok / named | where it lives here |
|---|---|---|
| question | 9 / 9 | the `question` family |
| Goal | 10 / 10 | the `goal` family |
| Todo | 4 / 4 | the `todo` family |
| child | 15 / 15 | Child work is `agent` here — a spawned subagent — plus the crew that fans several out and the thread-level spawn that gives one its own conversation. |
| activity | 14 / 14 | the `activity` family |
| diff | 3 / 3 | the `diff` family |
| artifact | 7 / 7 | the `artifact` family |

| offline/replay | 6 / 6 | The `sync` family: go offline, queue a send, reconnect, replay the queue idempotently, reconcile a snapshot, and pick up work the server did while away. |
| BSD | 9 / 9 | the `bsd` family |
| attachment | 8 / 8 | the `attachment` family |
| recovery | 9 / 9 | Recovery is not one family — it is what several families do after a failure, so it is listed as the retry/repair/restore path of each: a failed child retried, a failed artifact retried, a broken provider repaired, a dropped connection replayed, a thread rewound to a restore point, and the Director reset. |

## 4. Activity flow — the pixel probe

This is the section the packet's correction exists for. `03_compact_execution_activity.mov` is
reproduced as behaviour in all eight thread concepts, and the probe asserts the RENDERED result
at each beat rather than counting dispatches — the specific failure mode that let a previous
build report motion the DOM never performed.

| concept | capsule | **chain rendered** | **glyph count matched state every beat** | **header held still on every count tick** | count ticks observed | **every glyph reopens its phase** | **every glyph opens to its own headline** | sentence row follows open phase | sentence row via | glyphs probed | handovers observed | handover clears before new glyph | handover order visible across frames | handover beats |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| t1 | `t1-run` | yes | yes | yes | 2 | yes | yes | yes | `run-head` | 3 | 2 | yes | yes | `read-1`, `edit` |
| t2 | `t2-run` | yes | yes | yes | 2 | yes | yes | **NO** | `parent of run-verb` | 3 | 2 | yes | **NO** | `read-1`, `edit` |
| t3 | `t3-run` | yes | yes | yes | 2 | yes | yes | yes | `run-head` | 3 | 2 | yes | yes | `read-1`, `edit` |
| t4 | `t4-run` | yes | yes | yes | 2 | yes | yes | yes | `run-sentence` | 3 | 2 | yes | yes | `read-1`, `edit` |
| t5 | `t5-run` | yes | yes | yes | 2 | yes | yes | yes | `run-head` | 3 | 2 | yes | yes | `read-1`, `edit` |
| t6 | `t6-run` | yes | yes | yes | 2 | yes | yes | yes | `run-head` | 3 | 2 | yes | yes | `read-1`, `edit` |
| t7 | `t7-run` | yes | yes | yes | 2 | yes | yes | yes | `run-head` | 3 | 2 | yes | yes | `read-1`, `edit` |
| t8 | `t8-run` | yes | yes | yes | 2 | yes | yes | **NO** | `run-sentence` | 3 | 2 | yes | yes | `read-1`, `edit` |

Bold column headings are the EXIT GATE — a `NO` there is a defect. The rest are recorded and
deliberately not gated, because a concept whose layout differs from one reference geometry has
made a choice, and scoring the choice as a failure would be measuring conformity rather than
the product. The distinction comes from the measurement itself (`gatedVerdictKeys`), so this
summary cannot drift from the exit code it describes.

All eight pass every gated verdict. Recorded, non-gating differences, with the reason each is
recorded rather than failed:

- **t2**, `sentenceRowFollowsOpenPhase` — Whether the NARROW sentence row tracks the opened phase. t2 has no header row at all — its sentence lives on the subject phase’s own chip — and t8 puts the opened phase in its footnote by design, so its line describes the run while the footnote describes the phase. Both read false here and both are correct; the capsule read above is the one that gates.
- **t2**, `handoverOrderVisibleAcrossFrames` — The same order asked about TIME: did a frame exist in which the sentence had gone and the glyph had not yet arrived? A concept can be true above and false here, which means it wrote the mutations in the right order INSIDE one frame — correct, and invisible. That is what t2 reports, and it is a consequence of t2 being the one concept that keeps element identity.
- **t8**, `sentenceRowFollowsOpenPhase` — Whether the NARROW sentence row tracks the opened phase. t2 has no header row at all — its sentence lives on the subject phase’s own chip — and t8 puts the opened phase in its footnote by design, so its line describes the run while the footnote describes the phase. Both read false here and both are correct; the capsule read above is the one that gates.

Evidence: PNGs in `evidence/`, named `activity-t{N}-{NN}-{beat}.png`, clipped to the run
capsule where one exists.

## 5. Question paging

`02_stable_paged_questionnaire.mov` is a REVIEWABLE questionnaire: you page back, the answer is
still there, and the card does not replay its entrance. Its card also only looks stable because
every one of its pages carries four option rows — ours genuinely differ, so the card resizes
instead, using the bounce from PMConcept7's own model picker.

| concept | root | forward | back | same root throughout | entrance replayed going back | answer still shown | heights |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| t1 | `.t1-qturn` | 3 | 3 | yes | no | yes | 162 / 168 / 168 / 138 / 168 / 168 / 162 |
| t2 | `.t2-capsule` | 3 | 3 | yes | no | yes | 122 / 102 / 102 / 131 / 102 / 102 / 122 |
| t3 | `.t3-qrun` | 3 | 3 | yes | no | yes | 159 / 159 / 159 / 189 / 159 / 159 / 159 |
| t4 | `.t4-qdigest` | 3 | 3 | yes | no | yes | 1 / 87 / 87 / 87 / 87 / 87 / 87 |
| t5 | `.t5-qlane[data-lane="user"]` | 3 | 3 | yes | no | yes | 82 / 82 / 82 / 91 / 98 / 82 / 82 |
| t6 | `.t6-form` | 3 | 3 | yes | no | yes | 142 / 160 / 195 / 212 / 186 / 212 / 212 |
| t7 | `.t7-deck` | 3 | 3 | yes | no | yes | 152 / 155 / 134 / 152 / 134 / 134 / 149 |
| t8 | `.t8-qnote` | 3 | 3 | yes | no | yes | 148 / 159 / 155 / 144 / 155 / 155 / 162 |

The height column is the evidence that the bounce has something to animate: a card whose height
never changed would be a resize primitive wired to nothing, which is the failure this workspace
has produced three times and now tests for.

The folder scan (`node tools/drive.mjs scan`) is a separate gate and is not summarised here. It
checks four things and exits non-zero on any hit: no source file carries a NUL byte or fails
UTF-8 decode; no forbidden provider-acquisition phrase appears anywhere in the folder; no emoji
or pictograph appears in any file, comments and strings included; and every `cmd.*` id named in
surface source, in `candidate-wiring-delta.json` or in `plan-owner-delta.md` is recorded in
`candidate-command-delta.json`, so no surface can print a command the catalog owner has not been
shown.
